practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following was the first temporary President of the Constituent Assembly of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, the oldest member, was elected as the temporary President of the Constituent Assembly following the French practice on December 9, 1946. Later, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent President.

practiceQuestions.q: In which year was the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India put forward for the first time by M. N. Roy?
practiceQuestions.sol: In 1934, the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India was put forward for the first time by M. N. Roy, a pioneer of the communist movement in India.

practiceQuestions.q: Who presented the historic 'Objectives Resolution' in the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the historic 'Objectives Resolution' in the Assembly on December 13, 1946. It laid down the fundamentals and philosophy of the constitutional structure.

practiceQuestions.q: How many members were initially assigned to the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Drafting Committee, set up on August 29, 1947, consisted of seven members: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar (Chairman), N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, Dr. K. M. Munshi, Mohammad Saadulla, N. Madhava Rau, and T. T. Krishnamachari.

practiceQuestions.q: When was the National Flag of India adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Flag of India on July 22, 1947, a few days before India's independence from British rule.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was appointed as the Constitutional Advisor (Legal Advisor) to the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sir B. N. Rau was appointed as the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly. He prepared the initial draft of the Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: How much time did the Constituent Assembly take to finalize the Constitution of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constituent Assembly took 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days to frame the Constitution, during which it held 11 sessions spread over 165 days.

practiceQuestions.q: Who headed the Provincial Constitution Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel headed the Provincial Constitution Committee as well as the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas.

practiceQuestions.q: When did the Constitution of India finally come into full force?
practiceQuestions.sol: While provisions relating to citizenship, elections, provisional parliament, etc., came into force on November 26, 1949, the rest of the Constitution came into force on January 26, 1950.

practiceQuestions.q: Who served as the Chief Draftsman of the Constitution in the Constituent Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: S. N. Mukherjee was the chief draftsman of the constitution in the Constituent Assembly. Prem Behari Narain Raizada was the calligraphist of the Indian Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: Why was January 26 specifically chosen as the date for the inauguration of the Constitution of India?
opts: It was the day the Constituent Assembly was first convened.
It commemorated the Lahore Session Congress resolution of Purna Swaraj in 1930.
It was mandated by the Indian Independence Act of 1947.
It coincided with the signing of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
practiceQuestions.sol: January 26 was specifically chosen because it was on this day in 1930 that Purna Swaraj day was celebrated, following the resolution of the Lahore Session (December 1929) of the INC.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following best explains the nature of representation in the Constituent Assembly formed in 1946?
opts: Directly elected by universal adult franchise.
Directly elected by the British Parliament.
Partly elected and partly nominated, based on the Cabinet Mission Plan.
Appointed solely by the Viceroy of India.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constituent Assembly was not directly elected by the people on the basis of adult franchise; rather, it was a partly elected and partly nominated body under the Cabinet Mission Plan. Members were elected indirectly by provincial legislative assemblies.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Indian Independence Act of 1947 fundamentally alter the status and powers of the Constituent Assembly?
opts: It dissolved the Constituent Assembly and created a new Parliament.
It made the Assembly a fully sovereign body and a dual-purpose legislative body.
It subjected all constitutional decisions to the veto of the British Crown.
It restricted the Assembly exclusively to making laws for British provinces only.
practiceQuestions.sol: The 1947 Act made the Assembly a sovereign body (free to frame any constitution and repeal British laws) and gave it a dual role: making the constitution (Chair: Dr. Rajendra Prasad) and enacting ordinary laws for the country (Chair: G. V. Mavalankar).

practiceQuestions.q: Why were the Muslim League members absent from the initial meetings of the Constituent Assembly?
opts: They were barred by the British government.
They boycotted the assembly, demanding a separate constituent assembly for Pakistan.
They failed to win any seats in the provincial elections.
They opposed the principle of universal adult franchise.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Muslim League boycotted the Constituent Assembly and insisted on a separate state of Pakistan, which led to the reiteration of the demand for partition.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of the Cabinet Mission Plan with regard to the grouping of provinces?
opts: It divided India into four administrative zones directly ruled by the Viceroy.
It grouped British provinces into three sections (A, B, and C) to address communal representation concerns.
It abolished all provincial boundaries and created a unitary state.
It allowed princely states to form a separate federation outside British India.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Cabinet Mission proposed grouping British provinces into Section A (Hindu-majority), Section B (Muslim-majority in northwest), and Section C (Muslim-majority in northeast) to accommodate the Muslim League's fears while keeping India united.

practiceQuestions.q: Which principle was adopted for the allocation of seats to British provinces in the Constituent Assembly?
opts: Equal representation for all provinces regardless of population.
Proportional representation based on population (roughly 1 seat for every 1 million).
Representation solely based on tax-paying capacity and educational qualifications.
Nomination by the provincial governors and the Viceroy.
practiceQuestions.sol: Seats were allocated to each British province in proportion to their respective population, roughly translating to one seat for every million people.

practiceQuestions.q: How were the representatives of Princely States chosen in the Constituent Assembly?
opts: Through direct elections held in the princely states.
By nomination by the heads of the princely states.
Elected by the elected legislative councils of princely states.
Appointed directly by the British Crown.
practiceQuestions.sol: The representatives of the princely states were to be nominated by the heads of the princely states, which explains why princely states initially stayed away and joined the Assembly progressively.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the prime constitutional significance of the 'Objectives Resolution' moved by Nehru?
opts: It served as the blueprint for the Preamble of the Indian Constitution.
It created the office of the President of India.
It defined the borders of India and Pakistan.
It abolished the princely states and integrated them into the Union.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Objectives Resolution provided the philosophical foundation and ideals (such as sovereignty, justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity) that ultimately shaped the Preamble and the core provisions of the Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the Drafting Committee considered the most critical committee of the Constituent Assembly?
opts: It had the largest number of members from the Muslim League.
It was entrusted with the task of preparing the draft of the new Constitution based on various proposals.
It had the sole power to veto any law passed by the provisional parliament.
It was appointed directly by the British Prime Minister.
practiceQuestions.sol: Tasked with preparing the draft of the new Constitution, the Drafting Committee evaluated proposals from various committees, resulting in the comprehensive document presented to the Assembly.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Constituent Assembly function to ensure broad consensus and democratic decision-making?
opts: Through strict party whips and majority voting alone.
Through exhaustive public debate, detailed scrutiny by committees, and preference for consensus over division.
By delegating all drafting work to British legal experts.
By keeping all deliberations secret from the general public.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Assembly operated through extensive public debate, meticulous committee work, and a spirit of accommodation and consensus, ensuring minority rights and regional aspirations were respected.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition of the Constituent Assembly:
1. The total strength of the Constituent Assembly was to be 389 under the Cabinet Mission Plan.
2. Out of this, 93 seats were allotted to the Princely States and 296 seats to British India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Cabinet Mission Plan (1946) fixed the total strength of the Constituent Assembly at 389, with 296 seats for British India and 93 seats for the Princely States.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the major committees of the Constituent Assembly and their heads:
1. Union Powers Committee - Jawaharlal Nehru
2. Steering Committee - Dr. Rajendra Prasad
3. Committee on Fundamental Rights - Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All pairs are correctly matched. Jawaharlal Nehru headed the Union Powers Committee and Union Constitution Committee; Dr. Rajendra Prasad headed the Steering Committee and Rules of Procedure Committee; Sardar Patel headed the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities, Tribal and Excluded Areas.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the elections to the Constituent Assembly in 1946:
1. The elections were held on the basis of universal adult franchise.
2. The seats allocated to each British province were divided among three principal communities: Muslims, Sikhs, and General.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because elections were not held on the basis of universal adult franchise; franchise was limited based on property, tax, and education. Statement 2 is correct; seats were distributed among Muslims, Sikhs, and General (all others) in proportion to their population.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the functioning of the Constituent Assembly as a Parliament:
1. The Constituent Assembly became the first Parliament of independent India (Dominion Legislature).
2. Whenever the Assembly met as the Constituent body it was chaired by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because when the Assembly met as a constituent body it was chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad, and when it met as a legislative body, it was chaired by G. V. Mavalankar.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the historic enactments and adaptations done by the Constituent Assembly:
1. It adopted the National Anthem on January 24, 1950.
2. It elected Dr. Rajendra Prasad as the first President of India on January 26, 1950.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Constituent Assembly held its final session on January 24, 1950, during which it adopted the National Anthem, National Song, and elected Dr. Rajendra Prasad as the first President of India.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the criticisms faced by the Constituent Assembly:
1. Critics argued that the Constituent Assembly was not a representative body because its members were not directly elected by the universal adult franchise.
2. Critics also claimed that the Assembly was dominated by Hindus and represented a single-party body (Congress).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements reflect common criticisms leveled against the Constituent Assembly. However, defenders pointed out that elections were held through indirect provincial representation reflecting community proportions, and members from diverse backgrounds and parties were included.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 1946 elections and the Constituent Assembly:
1. The Indian National Congress won 208 seats, while the Muslim League won 73 seats.
2. Mahatma Gandhi and M. A. Jinnah were both members of the Constituent Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because neither Mahatma Gandhi nor M. A. Jinnah were members of the Constituent Assembly. Gandhi stayed away, focusing on communal harmony.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the legal and institutional antecedents of the Indian Constitution:
1. The Government of India Act of 1935 provided the bulk of the administrative framework and details for the Constitution of India.
2. The Constitution-makers totally discarded foreign legal models and relied purely on ancient Indian texts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; the GoI Act 1935 heavily influenced the administrative details. Statement 2 is incorrect because the makers borrowed extensively from multiple foreign constitutions (USA, UK, Ireland, Canada, Australia, etc.).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the role of Dr. B. R. Ambedkar in the Constituent Assembly:
1. He was elected to the Constituent Assembly from West Bengal initially.
2. Following the partition of India, he was re-elected from the Bombay Presidency.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Ambedkar was first elected from the Jessore-Khulna constituency (East Bengal, which went to Pakistan). Statement 2 is incorrect because after partition, he was re-elected from the Bombay legislative assembly (Bombay Presidency), not vice versa.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the adoption and enforcement of the Constitution of India:
1. The Constituent Assembly ceased to exist as a constitution-making body on November 26, 1949, transforming into a provisional parliament.
2. The title of the Constitution ('The Constitution of India') is explicitly declared under Article 393 of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Constituent Assembly did not cease to exist on Nov 26, 1949; it continued as the provisional parliament of India until the first general elections in 1951-52. Statement 2 is correct; Article 393 states that this Constitution may be called 'The Constitution of India'.
